ex.sales: Someone asks about laser eye surgery pricing at night; the agent answers from the approved price sheet, offers consultation slots and logs the enquiry for the coordinator.
ex.marketing: The agent drafts a flu-season recall email for all patients due a check-up, using only appointment data, for the practice manager to approve.
ex.support: A patient asks whether to fast before a blood test; the agent answers from the lab's approved instructions and offers to connect a nurse for anything else.
ex.content: A physician's notes on knee-replacement recovery become a two-page, sixth-grade-reading-level handout for review.
ex.finance: The agent spots 40 claims denied for a missing modifier, groups them and drafts corrections for the billing team.
ex.hr: For a registered nurse opening, the agent checks each CV for an active licence and shift availability and summarises evidence for the recruiter.
ex.ops: A cancellation at 10am triggers a text to the next three waitlisted patients, and the first to confirm is booked.
ex.it: A nurse locked out of the EHR at shift change verifies with MFA and the agent unlocks the account under the runbook.
ex.legal: The agent lists renewal dates, liability caps and data-handling clauses from 30 vendor BAAs into one table for counsel.
ex.data: Every Monday the agent reports no-show rate by clinic and weekday with the query used, so managers can adjust reminders.

kpis: Missed appointments as a share of booked visits
Minutes to answer portal and SMS questions
faq: Is an AI agent HIPAA compliant?

The agent itself is not compliant or non-compliant; your setup is. Use vendors that sign a business associate agreement, limit the protected health information the agent sees, log access, and keep clinical decisions with licensed staff.
